summary.text: A 14-year-old girl with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes, diagnosed at age 10 with hyperglycemia, sweating, polyuria, polydipsia and fatigue, had negative type 1 autoantibodies and monogenic diabetes genetic testing, a mildly thinned heterogeneous pancreas on ultrasound and normal fecal elastase, lipase and pancreatic amylase. She was born full term after a pregnancy complicated by gestational diabetes; maternal grandparents had T2D and her mother had thyroid cancer.

At her first visit she was in good general condition with obesity (BMI 30 kg/m²) and acanthosis nigricans on the neck and armpits, on multiple daily insulin (glargine 9 U, lispro 12 U) with HbA1c 8.5%. Insulin was reduced and metformin started, then insulin was gradually stopped and metformin increased to 2 g per day with a hypocaloric diet, dietitian consultations and 10 hours per week of physical activity; after 12 months weight fell by 10 kg (BMI 30 to 26.4 kg/m²) and HbA1c was 7.4%.

One year later glycemic control remained suboptimal (TIR 61% in the text, 62% in Table 1), so empagliflozin 10 mg daily was started with metformin for persistent hyperglycemia. After six months HbA1c decreased from 7.4% to 6.2% and TIR rose to 91%, with a stable weight of 75 kg and BMI 26.2 kg/m². No adverse events such as diabetic ketoacidosis or genital infections were reported, renal function was normal, and blood pressure did not change meaningfully; Table 1 follow-up continues to the last visit.
